Omar: We are here to address the six-week shipping delay on microcontroller chips from our overseas supplier. Hassan: Given the six-week delay, I strongly recommend we halt production entirely until the primary shipment arrives. Mariam: I completely disagree with halting production. Mariam: If we stop production, we will violate our SLA delivery deadlines with our top three retail clients. Hassan: Continuing to run an idle line costs us twenty thousand dollars a week in factory overhead. Bilal: Halting is too extreme, but we could source alternative microcontrollers from a domestic supplier right away. Hassan: The domestic supplier charges forty percent more per unit and their component failure rates are higher, which is a huge concern. Mariam: The domestic price premium is still far cheaper than the financial penalties for missing our client delivery dates. Bilal: The domestic supplier also confirmed they have certified components that meet our technical specifications. Omar: I agree with Mariam and Bilal that missing customer commitments is our biggest risk. Omar: The decision is to procure five thousand microcontroller units from the domestic supplier to maintain ongoing assembly. Hassan: I accept that decision, though the added procurement expense will compress our gross margin. Bilal: I will request a binding quotation from the domestic supplier by tomorrow at noon. Mariam: I will inform our retail clients about our confirmed fulfillment timeline by Thursday. Omar: We must hold another meeting this Friday to finalize the purchase order details. Hassan: I agree that another session on Friday is necessary. Omar: Meeting adjourned.

Bilal: Perfect, since no specific deadlines are set today, we need another meeting next week to review progress and the architecture draft.
Zainab: Sounds good, see you all in the follow-up meeting.
